title: Grossglockner, Timmelsjoch and the Tyrolean Toll Roads
subRegion: Hohe Tauern, Zillertal, Ötztal and the Silvretta

bestPeriod.note: The high toll roads open between late May and mid-June and shut with the first serious snowfall, usually late October.

summary: A week of Austria's paying mountain highways — Zillertal, Grossglockner, Timmelsjoch and the Silvretta — driven in the right direction at the right hour.
hook: Austria charges money for its finest roads, and they are worth the money. This week links five private mountain highways and half a dozen free passes across Tyrol, Salzburg and Carinthia. Distances are short and times are long: 40 km of hairpins eats ninety minutes, and that is the point.

snapshot.Base(s): Mayrhofen (2 nights), Bruck an der Grossglocknerstrasse (1), Heiligenblut (1), Sölden (2)
snapshot.Best Period: July–September; mid-June and October are viable but pass-dependent
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: approx. 1,350 km; sustained alpine hairpins, gradients to 14%, max altitude 2,829 m
snapshot.Getting There: Fly to Innsbruck (INN); Munich (MUC) is 2h15 away and usually cheaper
snapshot.Who It Suits: Drivers who enjoy the driving, plus passengers who like glaciers and cake

itinerary.title: Inn valley out, Ziller valley up
itinerary.morning: Collect the car at Innsbruck airport. Before leaving the bay, confirm the digital Vignette is registered to the plate and that the agreement permits Italy. Head east on the A12 Inntalautobahn.
itinerary.afternoon: Leave at Wiesing for the B169 Zillertalstrasse, a flat busy valley road; stop at Zell am Ziller, then on to Mayrhofen at 630 m, where the valley splits into four. Mayrhofen's centre is short-stay metered, so use the hotel garage.
itinerary.evening: Walk the Hauptstrasse and plan tomorrow around the forecast rather than the itinerary.
itinerary.dayStats: 85 km · 1h20 driving · no passes · max altitude 630 m.

itinerary.title: Zillertaler Höhenstrasse and the Schlegeis dam
itinerary.morning: Drive down-valley to Ried im Zillertal and turn up the **Zillertaler Höhenstrasse**, a 48 km private panorama road running along the western flank to Hippach. Toll approx. €11 per car, ticket sold at the barrier. It is single-lane in places with passing bays, gradients to 13%, and it tops out near the Melchboden at about 2,020 m. Caravans and vehicles over 3.5 t are barred. Drive it north to south so the Tux valley and the glacier sit ahead of you.
itinerary.afternoon: Back in Mayrhofen, take the **Schlegeis Alpenstrasse**: 13 km, toll approx. €13, gates open roughly 05:30–22:00 and shut overnight. Two unlit tunnels, gradients around 10–14%, and a finish at the Schlegeisspeicher at 1,782 m under the Hochfeiler. The dam-crest car park fills from 10:30 in August; the lower Zamsergrund lot is the overflow and adds a 15-minute walk.
itinerary.evening: Return to Mayrhofen. The light on the Schlegeis is better at 17:00 anyway.
itinerary.dayStats: 120 km · 3h10 driving · 2 toll roads, 0 through-passes · max altitude 2,020 m.

itinerary.title: Gerlos Alpenstrasse to the Pinzgau
itinerary.morning: Head up the Gerlos valley on the B165 and pay the **Gerlos Alpenstrasse** toll (approx. €12 per car) for the panorama section between Gerlospass, 1,507 m, and Krimml. This is the one you drive for the descent: the road swings out onto the Krimmler Achental with the falls in the windscreen. Use the signed Wasserfall-Blick layby rather than stopping on the carriageway.
itinerary.afternoon: Park at Krimml and walk the lower cascades of the Krimmler Wasserfälle (entry approx. €8; 45 minutes to the first platform). Then run the flat Salzach valley east through Mittersill.
itinerary.evening: Sleep at Bruck or Fusch, ten minutes from the Ferleiten toll gate. Fill the tank tonight; there is no fuel above the gate.
itinerary.dayStats: 130 km · 2h30 driving · 1 pass (Gerlospass) · max altitude 1,507 m.

itinerary.title: Grossglockner Hochalpenstrasse
itinerary.morning: Be at the **Ferleiten** gate by 07:00. The **Grossglockner Hochalpenstrasse** is 48 km from Bruck to Heiligenblut, 36 hairpins, gradients up to 12%, and a day ticket of approx. €46.50 per car (motorcycles around €31). Gates open 05:30 in high summer and close to uphill traffic in the evening — roughly 21:00 in July, earlier from September; the road is shut overnight. Climb through Piffkar and Hochmais to **Fuscher Törl** at 2,428 m.
itinerary.afternoon: Take the 1.7 km cobbled spur to **Edelweissspitze**, 2,571 m — the highest point you can drive to on the road. It is narrow, one-and-a-bit lanes, with a small circular car park that holds perhaps forty cars and no turning room for anything long; if there is a queue at the bottom, come back after 16:00. Then Hochtor tunnel at 2,504 m and the branch road to **Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe**, 2,369 m, facing the Pasterze glacier. Its multi-storey Parkdeck genuinely fills between 10:30 and 15:00 in August, after which traffic is turned back at Guttal; arriving before 09:30 or after 16:00 solves it.
itinerary.evening: Drop to Heiligenblut, 1,301 m, and look back at the Glockner from the churchyard of St. Vinzenz.
itinerary.dayStats: 75 km · 3h30 driving · 2 passes (Hochtor, Fuscher Törl) · max altitude 2,571 m.

itinerary.title: Second crossing, then north to the Ötztal
itinerary.morning: Keep yesterday's ticket: the road sells a discounted second run within a set window, so cross northbound early while the Fuscher Lacke is still glassy.
itinerary.afternoon: Down to Bruck, then Zell am See, over **Pass Thurn** at 1,274 m to Kitzbühel, and along the B170 to Wörgl. Rejoin the A12 west past Innsbruck and turn up the B186 Ötztalstrasse at Ötztal-Bahnhof.
itinerary.evening: Arrive Sölden, 1,368 m, for two nights. Hotel garages are standard; street parking is scarce.
itinerary.dayStats: 295 km · 4h45 driving · 3 passes (Hochtor, Fuscher Törl, Pass Thurn) · max altitude 2,571 m.

itinerary.title: Timmelsjoch and the Jaufen loop
itinerary.morning: Drive south past Zwieselstein to the **Timmelsjoch Hochalpenstrasse**. The Austrian toll is approx. €22 per car; the road opens roughly early June to mid-October, runs 07:00–20:00 only, and is closed to vehicles over 3.5 t and to caravans in either direction. The Austrian ramp is smooth and wide; the summit at 2,509 m carries the Passmuseum, and the Italian descent to Moos in Passeier is the tight one — narrow, unlit tunnels and pitches to 13%.
itinerary.afternoon: Coffee in St. Leonhard in Passeier, then the **Jaufenpass**, 2,094 m, a free, well-graded South Tyrolean pass with 44 bends, into Sterzing/Vipiteno. Return north over the **Brennerpass**, 1,370 m. Take the free SS12/B182 over the top rather than the A22–A13 if you would rather look at Gossensass than pay the Brenner motorway's separate special toll on the Austrian side.
itinerary.evening: Back down the Wipptal to Sölden. This is the longest sustained mountain day of the week.
itinerary.dayStats: 215 km · 5h00 driving · 3 passes (Timmelsjoch, Jaufenpass, Brenner) · max altitude 2,509 m.

itinerary.title: Silvretta Hochalpenstrasse and out
itinerary.morning: Option A, and the better one if the day is clear: drive to the top of the **Ötztaler Gletscherstrasse** above Sölden — toll approx. €22, gates 07:00–17:00 — which reaches the Rettenbachferner car park at 2,829 m, the highest paved point in Austria. Then descend and run the Inn valley west to Landeck.
itinerary.afternoon: South from Landeck up the Paznaun to Galtür, then onto the **Silvretta Hochalpenstrasse**: 34 hairpins and gradients to 12% toward the Bielerhöhe. The lower Partenen ramp on the Vorarlberg side has been shut for rockfall barrier works since 2024 and stays closed until summer 2030, so in 2026 the road is driven as a toll-free there-and-back from Galtür (reopens for the season on 4 June) as far as the Vermuntsee. The Bielerhöhe at 2,032 m sits above the turquoise Silvretta-Stausee, with the Piz Buin behind it.
itinerary.evening: Retrace the Paznaun through Ischgl to Landeck, then back to Innsbruck.
itinerary.dayStats: 280 km · 4h45 driving · 2 passes (Bielerhöhe, plus the Gletscherstrasse spur) · max altitude 2,829 m.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Kramerwirt
accommodationStrategy.description: A centuries-old carved-timber Gasthof in the middle of Mayrhofen with its own garage, which matters because village surface parking is short-stay and enforced.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Senger
accommodationStrategy.description: An old shingled Kärntner farmhouse minutes below the Glockner road's southern gate, with parking on site and breakfast early enough to make the 07:00 barrier.
accommodationStrategy.booking: four months ahead; Heiligenblut has few beds.
accommodationStrategy.priceNote: €150–€230 per night for two, usually half board

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Regina
accommodationStrategy.description: Central Sölden, with an underground garage and both the Timmelsjoch and Gletscherstrasse gates ten minutes away. Summer rates here are a fraction of winter ones.

logistics.emergency: 112 pan-European. Austrian alpine rescue is **140**. Mountain-road breakdowns are recovered by ÖAMTC on 120.
logistics.weather: Afternoon storms build over the Hohe Tauern from about 14:00 in July and August. Check GeoSphere before the Glockner day and drive the high sections in the morning.

other.label: Vignette
other.text: A digital Vignette is compulsory on all Austrian Autobahnen and Schnellstrassen: roughly €13 for 10 days, €32 for two months, €107 for the year in 2026. Buy it from the ASFINAG shop or app, where it activates immediately; third-party resellers can impose a statutory withdrawal delay before validity begins. Rental cars from Austrian branches normally carry one — confirm at the desk.

other.label: Special tolls are separate
other.text: The Vignette buys nothing on the A13 Brenner, the A10 Tauern and Katschberg tunnels, the S16 Arlberg tunnel or the Felbertauerntunnel; each charges its own barrier fee. The five private mountain roads are separate again.

other.label: Cross-border and rentals
other.text: Austrian rentals allow Germany, Italy, Switzerland and Liechtenstein; several restrict travel further east, and cross-border fees of €25–€70 are normal. One-way drops abroad — Innsbruck to Munich — start around €100. Declare the Italy leg.

other.label: Emergencies
other.text: 112 pan-European. Austrian alpine rescue is **140**. Mountain-road breakdowns are recovered by ÖAMTC on 120.

other.label: Opening-hour traps
other.text: Grossglockner, Silvretta, Timmelsjoch, Schlegeis and the Gletscherstrasse all close their gates overnight; above a gate at closing you may descend but not re-enter. Village supermarkets shut at 18:00 and all Sunday.

other.label: Drone rule
other.text: Hohe Tauern National Park and the Grossglockner road prohibit drone launches; fines are real and the road company enforces them at Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe.

proTips: Buy the Grossglockner day ticket and use it twice. The road's discounted second-run ticket, taken the following morning, gives you the whole thing in reverse light for a fraction of the price.
The Edelweissspitze spur is the first thing to jam. Do it on the way *down* on your second Glockner crossing, not on the way up on your first.
Timmelsjoch's toll booth is on the Austrian side only. If you approach from Italy on a return leg you pay nothing, so plan the loop clockwise.
Fuel is cheapest in the valley towns — Zell am Ziller, Mittersill, Landeck. There is no fuel on any of the five toll roads, and Sölden's stations close early.

packingNotes: Polarising filter or sunglasses that kill glacier glare; the Pasterze at midday is brutal.
A fleece and a windproof — Edelweissspitze at 2,571 m can be 12°C colder than Mayrhofen.
Coins and small notes for barrier machines and Alm lunches.
Comfortable shoes for the Krimml falls and the Gamsgrubenweg; both involve wet rock.
Motion-sickness remedy for back-seat passengers. Thirty-six hairpins is not a metaphor.
whatCouldGoWrong: **A toll road opens late — or stays shut.** Snow can keep the Timmelsjoch shut into mid-June, and the Silvretta's Vorarlberg (Partenen) ramp is closed for construction until 2030, so 2026 access is Galtür-side only. Fallback: substitute the Kaunertaler Gletscherstrasse, which opens earlier and reaches 2,750 m, or run the Achensee and Kühtai loops instead.
**Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe car park is full.** Traffic is turned around at Guttal. Fallback: continue over Hochtor to Heiligenblut, drop the bags, and come back up in the evening on the same ticket.

**Rental refuses Italy.** Some Austrian franchises exclude it or charge on the spot. Fallback: skip Jaufen and Brenner, drive Timmelsjoch to the summit and back down, and add the Kühtaisattel on the return.
**Overnight gate closure catches you out.** Fallback: Heiligenblut, Galtür and Sölden all sit *below* their respective barriers — plan every night's bed on the valley side of a gate, never above one.
